problem.name: Local search on the Boolean hypercube
problem.statement_latex: Given value-oracle access to $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, output $x$ such that $f(x)\le f(x\oplus e_i)$ for every coordinate $i$, with probability at least $2/3$. Values have a finite comparison encoding. This models single-bit local improvement in combinatorial optimization. Complexity is measured in value-oracle queries for both quantum and randomized classical algorithms.
problem.statement_text: Given value-oracle access to $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, output $x$ such that $f(x)\le f(x\oplus e_i)$ for every coordinate $i$, with probability at least $2/3$. Values have a finite comparison encoding. This models single-bit local improvement in combinatorial optimization. Complexity is measured in value-oracle queries for both quantum and randomized classical algorithms.

quantum.headline_latex: $\Theta(2^{n/3}n^{1/6})$ queries, quantum sampling and local descent.
quantum.details_latex: Minimum finding selects a low-valued starting point, and quantum search finds improving neighbors. The bound is tight. On a fixed-dimensional grid with $N$ vertices and dimension at least six, the optimal quantum query complexity is $\Theta(N^{1/3})$.
quantum.headline_text: $\Theta(2^{n/3}n^{1/6})$ queries, quantum sampling and local descent.

classical.headline_latex: $\Theta(2^{n/2}n^{1/2})$ queries, randomized sampling and local descent.
classical.details_latex: The Aldous-type algorithm samples vertices, chooses the lowest sampled value, and follows improving neighbors. For a fixed-dimensional grid of dimension at least four, the tight randomized bound is $\Theta(N^{1/2})$.
classical.headline_text: $\Theta(2^{n/2}n^{1/2})$ queries, randomized sampling and local descent.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial speedup in the domain size $N=2^n$, with a smaller exponential constant in $n$. Minimum finding and amplitude amplification are algorithmic components.

evidence.description_latex: Matching quantum and randomized query lower bounds establish the separation.

hardware.description_latex: A fault-tolerant implementation needs an $n$-qubit vertex register, value and comparison workspace, and coherent neighborhood access. Exponentially many queries dominate the runtime; the evaluator determines the additional logical-qubit count.
